resultAnatomyFromCode.get_trending: One text content block: the edition line, then up to five headlines per section, each with source name and URL.
resultAnatomyFromCode.search_literature: One text content block: the answer text; then, when the answer was assembled from source excerpts or the pipeline degraded, one plain quality note saying so; then a Sources section of numbered lines (title, authors, year, DOI or URL, and whether the source was cited in the answer or is further reading); then a Coverage line (records gathered and sources cited) when the payload carries a funnel; then a coverage note when present. With no sources, the text says plainly that the answer should be treated as ungrounded. No record object, no structuredContent, and no internal identifiers are returned.

serverInfo.transport: Stateless streamable HTTP, plain JSON bodies, no sessions, no server sent events

toolCallObservations.observed: Worked. Returned the 2026-10-13 edition: four sections (Biology & Medicine, Preprints, Physics & Chemistry, Space), five headlines each, each headline carrying its source name and the original story URL. Result isError false.

Four calls on 13 October 2026, spaced through the afternoon, with four different questions (bees and stinging, frogs surviving freezing, sleep and colds, plants folding their leaves). All four returned successful results with isError false: one full synthesized answer (short answer first, disagreement and confidence sections, numbered citations) and three extractive answers in the What the sources say shape, which is the mode the endpoint serves when the synthesis fleet is capped; the result text discloses its assembly honestly. No call in this session returned the runner's fallback error text. A direct POST to https://askcerebrum.org/api/search in the same window returned HTTP 200 and a full answer in about 18 seconds, so the search path is slow as well as functional. See the reliability note in README.md.
